correctness.rationale: For every odd p, k>=1, and each s modulo p^k, the first n>=1 with U_n(s)=0 exists and is counted. The Laurent identity for roots z,z^-1 with trace s yields U_ab(s)=U_a(s)U_b(V_a(s)). For nonzero discriminant mod p, Hensel roots lie in either a split unit or unramified norm-one cyclic group of order (p∓1)p^(k−1); the rank equals order(z²). Dividing the root counts by inversion gives phi(d) for d with nontrivial p-free part dividing m±=(p±1)p^(k−1)/2, with p-prime-part multiplicity correctly included. Singular traces s≡±2 mod p require ramified analysis: for p>=5 the exact formula ν_p(U_n(s))=ν_p(n) yields rank p^k for 2p^(k−1) residues; at p=3, U3(s)=s²−1 and V3 iteration give rank 3^max(1,k−ν3(s²−1)+1), yielding a tower with weights 2 at rank3 and 4*3^(a−2) for rank3^a, 2<=a<=k. These disjoint split/nonsplit/singular cases exhaust every trace, and the sums equal p^k. Independently recomputed exact first-zero histograms p=3 through k3; p=5,7 through k2; p=11 k1; all matched formulas. The valuation proof—not bounded enumeration—justifies all odd prime powers.
